_about: How the certificates lens reads the certificates of a footprint. A certificate is an asset of certificate_types reached from a controlled asset by a relation whose purpose is certificate_purpose (a service presenting it, a name it covers); certificate authority certificates (ca_field true) are skipped. fields names the content fields read. name_types are the assets a certificate covers. A certificate is reported when it has expired or expires within expiry_warning_days, when it was issued by its own subject, when its signature algorithm is one of weak_signature_algorithms (names as Go's crypto/x509 prints them; SHA-1 and MD5 signatures are no longer accepted by browsers), when its validity is longer than max_validity allows for the date it was issued (the CA/Browser Forum's Baseline Requirements cap it, on a schedule), and, for review, when it is a wildcard or covers names of other domains. A certificate whose ext_key_usage lists mark_certificates.usage is a mark certificate for Brand Indicators for Message Identification (BIMI): the certificate authority verified the organization and its mark, so it is listed with the details stored on its subject ContactRecord (reached by subject_label): the organization (organization_label), the trademark registration and LEI Identifiers (identifier_label, by id_type), the trademark office that is the registration's issuing authority (authority_label, to a ContactRecord whose organization_label names it), the BIMI record's logo (logo_label) and the mark properties. Add values here, not in Go code. authorities name the certificate authorities, so the same authority is counted once however a certificate names it: by its organization or by the common name of the issuing certificate (Let's Encrypt's R10, Amazon RSA 2048 M04). An issuer whose name contains one of an authority's match words, or equals one of its issuers (the short names of issuing certificates), is that authority; any other issuer keeps its own name and is not a public certificate authority (the private-ca-issuance ownership signal relies on this list). provider_managed_names are the names that mark a certificate a CDN or hosting provider manages for many customers (a name equal to one, or below it): such a certificate's names and keys say nothing about who owns the sites it covers, so the ownership signals that compare certificates skip it.
